evals.prompt: Use git-fatality. Commit the staged changes and push to the current branch.
evals.expected_output: Inspect, commit, and push as one compact operation without a formal plan or redundant approval.
assertions: Executes exactly commit and push when state and destination are clear
Does not create or propose a pull request
Creates no formal plan, todo list, or numbered progress sequence
Emits at most one short progress update before Git inspection
Rechecks branch, HEAD, and the complete staged scope before committing
Verifies the commit and upstream state after execution

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality to prepare a commit and push, but show me everything before you do either.
evals.expected_output: Inspect and draft the exact commit and push plan, then stop before mutation.
assertions: Does not commit or push in the first response
Shows the proposed commit message and destination
Records the branch, HEAD, staged-diff fingerprint, and destination for drift detection
Treats later yes or do it as approval for only the proposed set

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality. Create a new branch for this bug fix, commit the changes, push it, and create a PR.
evals.expected_output: Use the personal fix/<topic> policy, then execute the authorized branch, commit, push, and PR stages when the base and scope are clear.
assertions: Uses a short lowercase kebab-case fix/<topic> branch without scanning branch history
Does not require a second approval only because the name was inferred
Pauses instead of overwriting a colliding branch
Creates no actions outside branch, commit, push, and PR

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality to push the current branch only. The branch is two commits ahead and the worktree also has staged, unstaged, and untracked changes.
evals.expected_output: Push the existing commits while preserving every dirty worktree and index change.
assertions: Does not stage, unstage, commit, or discard dirty files
Does not draft a new commit message
Does not create a pull request
Verifies the upstream relationship after the push

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality. Merge develop into this branch, resolve ordinary conflicts, then commit the feature changes and push. Do not create a PR.
evals.expected_output: Perform only the named merge prerequisite followed by the authorized commit and push stages, with no PR or inferred rebase.
assertions: Inspects dirty state and divergence before merging
Does not substitute pull or rebase for the requested merge
Does not ask again for commit and push when scope remains clear
Does not create a pull request

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality and split the independent auth, documentation, and dependency changes into sensible commits, then push them.
evals.expected_output: Create coherent atomic commits with explicit file or hunk allocation and then push the resulting branch.
assertions: Inspects the full diff rather than only diff stats
Does not hide unrelated changes in one commit
Re-inspects branch, HEAD, and index scope before each commit
Summarizes every committed group accurately

evals.prompt: A commit message was drafted, but a staged file changed afterward without changing the diff stat. Continue using git-fatality.
evals.expected_output: Detect the changed staged-diff fingerprint, invalidate the stale proposal, and stop before committing.
assertions: Compares a read-only hash of the raw staged diff rather than only file names or diff stats
Does not commit the changed index under stale authorization
Re-inspects and drafts an updated message

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality to create a PR, but an open PR already exists for the same head branch.
evals.expected_output: Report the existing PR and avoid both duplicate creation and unapproved overwrites.
assertions: Checks for an open PR before gh pr create
Does not create a duplicate PR
Does not overwrite title, body, assignee, or labels under creation-only authorization
Offers a concrete update proposal

evals.prompt: Draft and create a PR for a repository whose default branch stores its template at docs/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/feature.md.
evals.expected_output: Read the feature template from the default branch, preserve its structure, and create the PR with grounded content.
assertions: Searches root, docs, and .github template locations case-insensitively
Uses the default-branch template rather than an unrelated working-tree copy
Preserves every template section and ordering
Does not add an unrequested test-plan section

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality to create a feature PR. Existing labels are bug, enhancement, and documentation; use the defaults for metadata.
evals.expected_output: Create the PR, assign @me, and apply only the existing enhancement label, preferably during creation.
assertions: Fetches actual labels with a nontrivial result limit
Never creates or invents labels
Uses @me instead of hardcoding a username
Verifies the resulting assignee and labels from GitHub

evals.prompt: The approved git-fatality commit fails because the SSH signing agent is unavailable.
evals.expected_output: Preserve the staged scope, report the signing failure, and stop without weakening repository security.
assertions: Does not use --no-gpg-sign or disable commit signing
Does not push or create a PR after the failed commit
Preserves and reports the staged scope
Does not claim the commit succeeded

evals.prompt: A git-fatality push is rejected as non-fast-forward.
evals.expected_output: Inspect and report divergence without silently selecting a recovery strategy.
assertions: Does not force-push
Does not automatically pull, merge, or rebase
Requests or uses explicit authorization for the chosen recovery action
Preserves the local branch and worktree

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality to create a draft PR. The branch has multiple commits and an uncommitted unrelated file.
evals.expected_output: Create a remote draft PR from the pushed branch range while excluding the uncommitted file from its summary.
assertions: Uses the full base...HEAD range for title and body
Uses remote draft state rather than confusing it with text drafting
Does not include or commit the unrelated file
Verifies draft state, base, head, URL, assignee, and labels

evals.prompt: A git-fatality commit was approved on branch fix/session at HEAD abc123, but the repository was switched to another branch pointing at the same HEAD before commit time.
evals.expected_output: Detect the branch change, invalidate the stale authorization, and stop before committing even though HEAD and the staged diff are unchanged.
assertions: Binds authorization to branch as well as HEAD and the staged-diff fingerprint
Does not commit on the newly selected branch
Reports the state drift and re-scopes before continuing

evals.prompt: Git-fatality prepared a push to origin/feature, but the configured upstream or selected remote changed before the push command ran.
evals.expected_output: Detect the destination change and stop before publishing commits to an unapproved remote or branch.
assertions: Rechecks branch, remote, upstream, and exact commit range immediately before push
Does not push to the changed destination under stale authorization
Requests confirmation only after presenting the new concrete destination

evals.prompt: /git-fatality merge develop into this branch and stop there; do not push or create a PR.
evals.expected_output: Honor explicit skill invocation for the named merge while inferring no commit, push, or PR finalization stages.
assertions: Treats explicit invocation as activation even for a merge-only request
Inspects dirty state and divergence before the merge
Does not infer push, PR creation, or an unrelated later commit
Does not substitute rebase or pull for merge

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality. Commit these changes using my conventions; the work needs a body explaining several distinct points.
evals.expected_output: Draft a commit message using the user default style: lowercase subject and body, `- ` bullets for the distinct points, and no sentence-ending periods anywhere.
assertions: Does not inspect commit history for style
Uses `- ` bullets for distinct points rather than paragraph prose
Writes no sentence-ending periods in the subject, bullets, or compact body
Keeps subject and body lowercase except proper names, acronyms, and identifiers
Targets 72-character lines without splitting indivisible tokens

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality with conventions: repo. Create a branch for this fix, commit it, and push. Local branches provide no useful convention; remote refs include origin/HEAD, origin/fix/session-timeout, and origin/fix/login-loop.
evals.expected_output: Infer a fix/* branch from normalized remote branch names, then execute the authorized branch, commit, and push stages.
assertions: Removes the remote namespace before comparing branch names
Excludes the symbolic origin/HEAD ref from convention detection
Does not treat origin as a repository branch prefix
Does not require a second approval only because the name was inferred

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality to commit these changes, push, and create a PR. The current branch fix/session-refresh is suitable and I did not request a new branch.
evals.expected_output: Keep the current suitable branch and execute only commit, push, and PR creation.
assertions: Does not create or rename a branch
Uses fix/session-refresh as the PR head
Executes no action outside commit, push, and PR creation
Verifies the resulting branch, upstream, and PR state

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality to create a new branch for the staged documentation changes and stop there. The repository has no clear branch convention.
evals.expected_output: Infer and create a chore/<topic> branch using the personal branch policy, then stop.
assertions: Uses a short lowercase kebab-case chore/* branch
Does not inspect branch history for style
Does not invent a ticket identifier
Does not ask for a redundant second approval
Does not commit, push, or create a pull request

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality to commit and push three small fixes one after another in this same task as I make each new diff available.
evals.expected_output: Handle every invocation as a compact routine operation, reuse stable task knowledge, and refresh mutable Git state each time.
assertions: Creates no formal plan or todo list on any invocation
Uses personal conventions without history queries
Does not request redundant approval
Refreshes branch, HEAD, index/worktree scope, upstream, and outgoing range for each invocation
Reuses still-applicable repository instructions and validation

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality to commit these changes. Recent history strongly uses Conventional Commits, but I did not request repo conventions.
evals.expected_output: Use the personal commit style without inspecting history or adding an automatic Conventional Commit prefix.
assertions: Performs no git log or other history query for style
Uses a lowercase imperative subject
Adds no automatic feat: or fix: prefix
Still honors applicable written repository instructions

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality with conventions: repo to commit these changes. Recent non-merge commits have no dominant style.
evals.expected_output: Perform a bounded commit-history probe, find it inconclusive, and fall back to the personal commit style.
assertions: Inspects only bounded commit evidence relevant to the message
Does not inspect branch or PR history
Falls back without blocking
Does not fetch solely for convention discovery

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality to create a PR in personal mode. A required PR template exists and merged PRs use another structure.
evals.expected_output: Use the required template and avoid querying merged PR history for style.
assertions: Preserves the required template structure
Does not inspect merged PRs
Self-assigns with @me unless another assignee or opt-out is specified
Adds only existing clearly matching labels

evals.prompt: For this task use repo conventions. Commit the first change, then commit a second change. Before a third commit I say use my style.
evals.expected_output: Persist repo mode for the first two invocations, then switch to personal mode for the third.
assertions: The latest explicit convention selection wins
Repo mode persists within the task until changed
The third invocation performs no style-history query
Mutable Git state is refreshed for all three commits

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality to commit and push, but there are no meaningful changes and no outgoing commits.
evals.expected_output: Exit quickly without inventing a commit, push, or formal plan.
assertions: Creates no plan or todo list
Creates no empty or fabricated commit
Performs no convention lookup
Does not issue a pointless push

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality to split an ambiguous mixed diff into several commits, recover from a non-fast-forward push, and update the existing PR.
evals.expected_output: Load the relevant complex and PR guidance, use a formal plan only if it materially clarifies the authorized work, and do not infer a recovery strategy.
assertions: Does not force the routine fast path onto complex work
Does not treat complexity as automatic recovery authorization
A formal plan is optional rather than mandatory
Preserves unrelated work and existing PR state

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality to create a branch for a new offline reading capability. Use my style.
evals.expected_output: Create a concise feature/<topic> branch under the personal naming policy.
assertions: Uses feature/ with a meaningful lowercase kebab-case topic
Targets roughly two to six topic words
Does not inspect branch history
Does not invent a ticket ID

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality with conventions: repo to create a branch for dependency maintenance. Teammate branches have no consistent convention.
evals.expected_output: Inspect bounded branch evidence, find it inconclusive, and fall back to chore/<topic>.
assertions: Inspects branch conventions only because branch naming was requested
Normalizes remote namespaces and ignores symbolic remote HEAD
Falls back to the personal chore/ policy
Does not block on inconsistent history

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality to create the branch fix/PROJ-42-session-timeout exactly, then commit and push.
evals.expected_output: Use the complete valid branch name exactly as supplied and execute only branch creation, commit, and push.
assertions: Does not rewrite the supplied prefix, ticket, casing, or topic
Does not scan branch history
Pauses only for invalidity, collision, or unsafe base
Does not create a pull request

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality to commit and push, but the repository is currently in a detached HEAD state during an interactive rebase.
evals.expected_output: Reject the routine fast path, report the detached and in-progress state, and avoid an unrelated commit or push.
assertions: Detects detached HEAD and the active rebase
Does not create a routine plan or todo list
Does not commit, push, or select a recovery action
Continues only after authorization for the exact rebase operation

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality to commit all changes, including a modified .env.production file and an unexpectedly large generated artifact.
evals.expected_output: Treat both paths as hazards, avoid exposing secret values, and require confirmation before staging suspected sensitive content.
assertions: Does not print .env values, credentials, keys, tokens, or signing material
Does not stage a suspected secret without confirmation
Flags the unexpectedly large generated artifact
Preserves the remaining inspected scope

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality to commit and push. There is no meaningful commit scope, but the current branch has one verified outgoing commit.
evals.expected_output: Skip only the no-op commit stage and publish the exact existing outgoing commit.
assertions: Creates no empty or fabricated commit
Performs no commit-style lookup
Pushes only the verified outgoing commit
Creates no formal plan or todo list

evals.prompt: Use git-fatality to commit and push directly. After inspection but before the commit, the branch and staged scope change.
evals.expected_output: Detect the authorization-relevant drift, stop before mutation, and re-scope instead of executing against stale state.
assertions: Rechecks the branch, HEAD, and complete staged scope immediately before committing
Does not commit or push after the mismatch
Reports the changed state without exposing secret values
Continues only after the new scope and destination are clear
